text:
mira: Heads-up — finalizing the Q3/Q4 platform roadmap doc. Need alignment on a few cross-cutting things: routing policy DSL, launch safety gates (canaries + rollback), and customer migration waves. Quick proposal: policy tiers (shielded / default / best-effort), region affinity hints, and transparent fallback rules.

sam: For prioritization we need concrete SLAs per tier. Suggest shielded = 99.95 uptime, P95 latency target 50ms; default = 99.9, P95 120ms; best-effort = no SLA but cost cap.

oliver: I sketched a minimal policy DSL to capture tier + region affinity + fallback. Example snippet below — lightweight, human-readable: 

```
policy "customer-xyz" {
  tier: "shielded"
  preferred_regions: ["us-west-2", "us-east-1"]
  fallback: { model_family: "gpt-compat", degrade_to: "best-effort" }
  canary: { percent: 5, duration_min: 60 }
}
```

oliver: DSL is intentionally small so product/legal can review quickly. It maps to route metadata we already emit.

tess: Sales note — two customers asked for "priority onramp" and want firm launch dates. They'll accept a canary but want a documented rollback plan + compensation clauses. I flagged for contract.

ana: From CS: both customers need data residency & audit logs. One requires single-region tenancy initially (us-east). We should include explicit residency gating in the checklist.

dev-bot: Reminder — design doc draft is in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood/platform-policy-dsl (permissions: product + eng).

li: Operational concerns: cross-region failover will invalidate KV caches unless we pin routing or add cross-region replication. Cost for replication is non-trivial — call it out in the pricing appendix. Also need chaos tests for cache eviction scenarios.

sam: +1 to calling out costs. Also: add quantization fallback/cheaper model path for best-effort tier to hit cost targets.

mira: Proposed launch criteria (short checklist):
  1) Policy DSL spec approved by product/infra/legal
  2) Canary harness + synthetic load tests (SLO validation)
  3) Migration playbook with rollback steps and runbook (ops + CS)
  4) Pricing appendix showing unit economics by tier
  5) Customer onramp checklist (data residency, kms, contract addendum)

oliver: One more: eviction safety net — automatic downgrade to a compatible smaller model (with quality warning) instead of request failure. Gives better availability at cost of quality.

tess: I'll escalate SLA/compensation ask to legal. @mira can you confirm target timeline for customer onramp? They want dates.

mira: Target: draft DSL + checklist by EOD Thu; canary + sim results by next Wed; onramp plan for the two customers by end of next week.

li: I'll own the failover sim — will schedule a run and post results in this thread.

ana: I'll confirm each customer's residency + audit requirements and return a matrix (region, KMS, log retention).

sam: I'll put numbers behind the SLA proposals and cost delta for reserved vs burst capacity.

mira: Action items recap: oliver -> PR for DSL spec (Thu EOD); sam -> SLA + econ numbers (next Wed); li -> failover sim (this week); ana -> customer constraints matrix (Tue); tess -> escalate legal/SLA (today). Sync: Thu 10:00am PT in #product-ops.

oliver: one question — do we want to allow per-route overrides (yes/no)? I vote yes but with guardrails.

sam: vote yes. Allows sales/solutions to pin a route when customer pays for it. Need strong telemetry.

mira: Agree — per-route overrides allowed behind an entitlement flag and accompanied by a rollout checklist.

mira: OK closing loop for now. If anyone wants to add to the checklist or DSL fields, put comments on the DSL PR. :thumbsup:
